text:
maya: running nsys on a prod-like distroless container; kernel timelines look fine but line info is missing for libredwood_runtime.so and a few system libs. nvtx/cupti events show up. anyone seen nsys fail to map debuginfo due to container build-id/pathmap mismatches?

tobias: did you check /usr/lib/debug inside the container? nsys needs build-ids to map to separate .debug files. packaging often strips and drops .debug elsewhere.

maya: yep — we build with -g in CI, then we strip in the packaging step. readelf shows a Build ID in the .so but /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/ is empty in the final image.

rene: try bind-mounting the host's /usr/lib/debug into the container when profiling. also verify the .gnu_debuglink and build-id: `readelf -n libredwood_runtime.so | grep Build` and `ls /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/`.

maya: repro I ran in a minimal way to illustrate the packaging problem:
```bash
# build stage
gcc -g -O2 -fPIC -c runtime.c -o runtime.o
gcc -shared -o libredwood_runtime.so runtime.o
# keep separate debug file then link it
strip --only-keep-debug libredwood_runtime.so libredwood_runtime.so.debug
objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink=libredwood_runtime.so.debug libredwood_runtime.so
# packaging step copies only libredwood_runtime.so into distroless image and drops .debug
```

kevin: packaging dropped the .debug files, yep. two practical fixes: 1) include the .debug files in the runtime image under /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/<id>/file.debug, or 2) avoid losing the link by using `eu-strip --keep-debug` / keep the separate .debug artifact and mount it during profiling.

tobias: if you can't change the image, another route is to run nsys from the host but target the container process (nsys can attach to PIDs), and make sure the host's build-id cache contains the container .debug files. alternatively run a lightweight debuginfod server that serves the .debug tarball and set DEBUGINFOD_URLS to point to it.

maya: i tried bind-mounting /hostdebug -> /usr/lib/debug inside the container, but nsys still reported 'no debug symbols' for some .so files under /opt/pack. it turned out our CI rewrote paths in the .gnu_debuglink entries to a relative layout that doesn't match the image root. so even though the .debug file existed, the debuglink couldn't be resolved.

rene: tools that helped me: `eu-readelf -n <so>`, `readelf --debug-dump=info <so>`, and `objdump -h <so>`. also `readelf --string-dump=.gnu_debuglink` to inspect debuglink names. CUPTI shows GPU activity but doesn't influence ELF debug mapping — making sure driver/toolkit versions match matters for kernel traces, but it's separate from symbol resolution.

maya: final fix i'm testing: ensure packaging emits the .debug file into the image at /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/<buildid>/, and add a CI artifact (debug tarball) uploaded to our debug artifact S3. then run debuginfod in ephemeral CI when profiling so nsys can fetch. with that change nsys now maps runtime.cpp:142 and hotspots show in the trace and perf timelines. :tada:

perf-bot: profile recorded -> s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1950123456.qdrep (meta: build=2026-03-17, image=distroless-v3)

kevin: nice work. follow-up: add a packaging checklist and a CI job that produces a debuginfod manifest + tarball so on-demand profiles can fetch matching debuginfo automatically.

maya: will open a PR with the packaging change and a short runbook for profiling containerized builds. thanks all :heart:
